ideas.name: Speed Strip
ideas.approachWhy: The idea is one clear move (run the strip, leap the gap) and every gap must be checked against the boosted jump, so a small hand-made set is safer and easier to test than a generator. Variants differ in what you do before the jump, not in random lengths.

have: Belt part and conveyor surface speed (GooConveyor)
slide motion for a moving landing pad
gap and rise checks in ObbyCourse.spec (8.7 stud walking jump, GAP_MAX 6)
red goo hazard look and reset on touch

new.what: Client boost controller: on a boost part, raise the local WalkSpeed to `power`, hold it `carry` s after you leave, then ease back to 16; a back strip lowers it to 10. A conveyor alone will not do: the character loses belt speed the moment it leaves the ground. Only new system this idea owns.
Boost look: reuse Arrow Maze's (#23) 'scrolling yellow chevron texture' on every boost strip (back strips scroll toward you), plus a whoosh, speed lines and a small view widen while fast

Boosted jump test: one shared 'launch reach' check with Ice Slide's (#6) slide-jump test and Bounce Chain's (#4) launchReaches(): each boosted gap must be over 8.7 studs (so it needs the boost) and within 80% of the boosted reach (speed 30 reaches about 16 studs, so gaps up to 13)
Blink Boost: reuse Glow Memory's (#10) 'Glow-only motion' (strip stays solid, glow on a timer) with the boost switched by the same timer, and the Beat Pads (#18) 'client beat clock' tick
Downhill Dash: reuse Ice Slide's (#6) 'Slope pieces' / Rolling Blobs' (#14) 'ramps' (one tilted-slab support, not a second one)
No Second Try: reuse Melting Floor's (#2) melt trigger 'melt when you leave (Burnt Bridge)' on the runway tiles

ideas.readability: Yellow strips with chevrons that scroll the way they push you (the same chevron texture as Arrow Maze belts, but these sit flat on solid floor and make you fast, not pushed), plus a whoosh, speed lines and a wider view while you are fast. Back strips have chevrons pointing at you and a low slow-down sound.

variants.name: First Boost
variants.does: One long yellow strip, then one gap you can only clear with its speed.
variants.numbers: strip 24 studs, boost 30, gap 11, landing 12 deep

variants.name: Downhill Dash
variants.does: The strip runs down a gentle slope and the landing sits lower, so you get extra air time.
variants.numbers: strip 20 studs at 8 deg down, boost 30, gap 12, landing 3 lower

variants.name: Up a Step
variants.does: The landing is 2.5 studs higher: boost, jump at the very edge and climb onto it.

variants.name: Stay in the Yellow
variants.does: A wide floor with only a middle stripe of boost: wander off it and you arrive too slow.
variants.numbers: floor 24 wide, strip 8 wide x 24 long, boost 30, gap 11

variants.name: Two Hops
variants.does: Two strip-and-gap pairs in a row; the landing of the first jump is the second strip.
variants.numbers: 2 strips x 16 studs, boost 30, gaps 10 and 10

variants.name: Wide Landing
variants.does: The longest jump in the easy tier, but onto a big landing so a late jump still counts.
variants.numbers: strip 28 studs, boost 30, gap 12.5, landing 20 deep x 24 wide

variants.name: Backwash
variants.does: The first stretch has chevrons pointing back that slow you down; hop over them to reach the real boost.
variants.numbers: back strip 8 studs (slows to 10), forward strip 14, boost 30, gap 11

variants.name: Carry the Speed
variants.does: A small plain hop sits between the strip and the long gap: keep moving so the boost does not run out.
variants.numbers: strip 16, boost 30 held 1.5 s, small gap 5, plain pad 6, long gap 11

variants.name: Stepping Boosts
variants.does: No long strip, just short boost pads with small gaps; each pad tops up your speed for the next.
variants.numbers: 4 pads x 5 studs, gaps 5, boost 30 held 1.2 s, last gap 12

variants.name: Hurdles
variants.does: Low red goo bumps sit on the strip; short hops over them keep the boost going.
variants.numbers: strip 26, 3 red bumps 1.5 high, boost 30, gap 11

variants.name: Sliding Landing
variants.does: Boost into a jump onto a platform that slides side to side; leave when it lines up with you.
variants.numbers: strip 20, boost 30, gap 11, target 10 x 10 sliding 6 studs over 3.2 s

variants.name: No Second Try
variants.does: The runway tiles melt a moment after you leave them, so you cannot back up for a second run-up: one boosted run, then the leap.
variants.numbers: 6 strip tiles x 4 studs, melt 0.6 s after you leave, boost 30, gap 11

variants.name: Blink Boost
variants.does: The strip glows and ticks on and off (it stays solid) and only boosts while lit, so start your run so you reach the edge while it is still lit.
variants.numbers: strip 18, lit 1.6 s then off 1.4 s, boost 32, gap 12.5

variants.name: Back-and-Forth
variants.does: Forward and backward strips take turns; jump each back strip, land on the next forward one, and end on a moving pad.
variants.numbers: 3 forward strips 8, 2 back strips 6, boost 32, last gap 13 to a pad sliding 5 studs

variants.name: Left, Right, Leap
variants.does: Two boost strips sit in opposite halves of the lane with red goo beside each; cut across a short plain floor at full speed, before the boost runs out, then make the long gap.
variants.numbers: 2 strips 10 wide x 16, red goo on the other half, plain cross-over 10 deep, carry 1.2 s, boost 32, gap 13

variants.name: Double Leap Climb
variants.does: Two boosted leaps, each one up a step, with only a short strip between them to rebuild speed.
variants.numbers: strip 20, gap 12 rise 2.5, strip 10, gap 13 rise 2.5, boost 34
